summary: Geoffrey Barstow specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Hampshire College, Kathmandu University (BA), the University of Virginia (PhD), and under Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche. He held posts at the University of Virginia (~2013) and Oregon State University (~2017).

Geoffrey Goble works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Virginia and a PhD from Indiana University Bloomington. In 2016, he was appointed Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Oklahoma.

Geoffrey Samuel works in religious studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Oxford and Cambridge under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, Peter J. Wilson, and Edmund Leach. He held posts at Otago, Newcastle (1978–2004), Lancaster, and Cardiff University, becoming Emeritus Professor in 2014.

Georg August Wallin (1811–1852) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was educated at Katedralskolan i Åbo (~1823–1829) and the University of Helsinki (~1829–1836), where he later held a post from ~1851 to 1852.

Georg Buddruss (1929–2021) specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt (Dr. phil.) under Paul Thieme and at the University of Tübingen. From 1963 to 1995, he served as professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz.

Georg Bühler (1837–1898) was an Indologist and linguist. Educated under Theodor Benfey, Raphael Kühner, and Heinrich Ludolf Ahrens, he earned a PhD from Göttingen. He held professorships at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai (1863–1880), and later the University of Vienna.
Georg Christoph Lichtenberg (1742–1799) worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at the University of Göttingen from ~1763 to ~1769 and subsequently held a post there from ~1770 until 1799.

Georg Curtius (1820–1885) was a linguist who studied at the University of Bonn and Humboldt University of Berlin under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, Christian Lassen, and Franz Bopp. He served as a professor at the University of Leipzig from 1862 to 1885.

Georg Ebers (1837–1898) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen, Frederick William University Berlin, and Jena, training under August Boeckh and Karl Richard Lepsius. He held academic posts at the University of Jena (1869–1870) and Leipzig (1870–1889).

Georg Forster (1754–1794) was an Indologist and naturalist educated at Saint Peter's School. He held posts as professor of natural history at Collegium Carolinum (1779) and Vilnius University (1784–1787), and served as librarian and professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1788–1793).

Georg Freytag (1788–1861) was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at the University of Göttingen and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy in Paris. He served at Göttingen (1811–1813), Königsberg (~1814–1815), and as professor of oriental languages at Bonn (1819–1861).

Georg Friedrich Grotefend (1775–1853) was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne, Thomas Christian Tychsen, and Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren, later serving as Director of Ratsgymnasium Hannover (1821–1849).
Georg Grimm (1868–1945) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He lectured on Buddhism at the University of Munich and founded the Altbuddhistische Gemeinde in 1921.

Georg Heinrich Bernstein (1787–1860) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Jena, Leipzig, Göttingen, and under Franz Bopp. He held posts at the University of Jena (PD 1811), Humboldt University of Berlin (1812), and the University of Breslau (ord. Professor 1820).

Georg Heinrich Ferdinand Nesselmann (1811–1881) was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, linguistic, and Indological studies. He earned his Ph.D. under Peter von Bohlen at the University of Königsberg, where he became PD (1838), ao. Professor (1843), and ordinary professor (1859).

Georg Huth (1867–1906) worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin and Leipzig under Ernst Windisch, Paul Deussen, Hermann Oldenberg, and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Berlin University (1891) and the Ethnological Museum of Berlin.

Georg Jacob (1862–1937) was a scholar of history and archaeology. Educated at Erlangen, Berlin, Strasbourg, Breslau, and Leipzig under Theodor Nöldeke and Heinrich Fleischer, he held posts at Greifswald, Halle, Erlangen (1901–1909), and Kiel University (1911–1929).

Georg Kaibel (1849–1901) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He held academic posts at the University of Rostock (~1879–1882), the University of Breslau (~1882–1883), the University of Greifswald (~1883–1886), and the University of Göttingen (~1897–1901).

Georg Ludolf Dissen (1784–1837) was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at the University of Göttingen from ~1803 to 1807, later holding academic appointments at the University of Marburg (~1812–1813) and the University of Göttingen (~1813–1837).

Georg Martin Dursch (1800–1881) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied theology and philosophy at the University of Tübingen and Oriental studies in Paris under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. In 1828, he became a professor at Johann-Vanotti-Gymnasium Ehingen.
